sections.h2: Where is Fridley, Minnesota, and what does its housing stock look like?
sections.html:
Fridley is a first-ring suburb in the southern tip of Anoka County, directly north of Minneapolis, with 30,829 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It became a village in 1949 and a city in 1957, and most of its growth came between 1950 and 1970. That timing means a large share of Fridley's housing dates from the postwar decades.

The city is long from north to south and narrow from east to west, following the Mississippi River and the highways beside it. It borders Minneapolis, Columbia Heights, New Brighton, Mounds View, Spring Lake Park, Blaine, Coon Rapids, Brooklyn Park and Brooklyn Center. Rice Creek crosses the middle of town, and East Moore, West Moore and Locke lakes sit inside the city limits. Land area is about 10.2 square miles.

The area was first called Manomin, after the Ojibwe word for wild rice. John Banfill became the first settler in 1847, and the Legislature renamed the township for Abram Fridley in 1879. East River Road still follows the old Red River oxcart trail.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show about Fridley homeowners and renters?
sections.html:
Fridley has a larger share of renters and lower home values than the other three cities in this part of the metro that the Census compares. The Census Bureau lists 63.0 percent of units as owner-occupied and a median value of $302,900 for 2020-2024. That leaves roughly 37 percent of households renting, so investors and landlords are a regular part of the buyer pool.

sections.h2: Which Fridley city code rules should a seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Fridley enforces exterior and yard standards that a buyer's inspector or the city may flag, so walk the property first. The city's code enforcement page lists the items it sees most often.

  • Grass and weeds taller than an average of ten inches draw a ten-day notice, and the city mows and bills the owner if it is not cut.
  • Driveways must be paved or hard-surfaced, and gravel driveways are not allowed.
  • Garbage, recycling and compost containers belong behind the front setback and may sit at the curb only from 5:00 PM the day before collection to 9:00 PM on collection day.
  • Vehicles parked outside need current tabs and must be street operable, and cars cannot park on grass.
  • Fences top out at four feet in the front yard and seven feet in side and rear yards.

When a violation is not fixed, the city can have a contractor correct it and add the cost to the property's taxes, or issue a citation with court fees of at least $300. An owner can appeal in writing to the City Clerk within 14 business days. Clearing open notices before a buyer's walk-through avoids last-minute credits.

sections.h2: Does a Fridley rental house need a city license when it sells?
sections.html:
Fridley licenses rental property, so a buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should expect to apply for a license. The city uses two license subtypes: single family covers one to three units, and multi-family covers four or more. Applications go through the CitizenServe portal.

The owner must list a physical address, not a PO box. If the owner lives more than 50 miles from the property, a local contact is required. New owners can upload their purchase documents with the application because the owner shown in the portal comes from Anoka County records, which update every one to two months. Questions go to Fridley rental licensing at 763-572-3616.

If you are selling a rental and want the transaction to move smoothly, bring a copy of the current license certificate and any inspection results to the table.

sections.h2: How do I stop and transfer the Fridley water account at closing?
sections.html:
Tell the city's Utility Billing Division before your closing date, using the Moving In/Out form or by phoning 763-572-3529. Staff need a meter reading on the day of closing to prepare the seller's final bill, and the account switches to the new owner as of that date.

  • Residential water has a fixed charge of $26.01 per quarter plus tiered volume rates in the city's 2026 schedule.
  • Sewer is billed on winter-quarter water use, and recycling is $11.60 per quarter for homes.
  • Weekly garbage service comes from a private hauler licensed by the city, separate from the city bill.

Unpaid utility charges can become a lien and be sent to Anoka County to be collected with next year's property taxes. Notices go out on or before October 1 for balances billed through July 31. A 10 percent late fee can apply to past-due accounts.

sections.h2: What schools, roads and employers draw buyers to Fridley?
sections.html:
Fridley Public Schools, Independent School District 14, run Fridley High School, Fridley Middle School, Hayes Elementary and Stevenson Elementary. Parts of the city fall in other districts: a small northern area is in Anoka-Hennepin District 11, an eastern area is in Columbia Heights District 13, and much of the north-northeast belongs to Spring Lake Park District 16. Check the district for the exact address when you write the listing.

Interstate 694 and Minnesota Highways 47 and 65 are the main roads, and the Northstar commuter rail line stops at the Fridley station. The Medtronic operational headquarters, Unity Medical Center, a Target distribution center and the BNSF Northtown rail yard are among the larger employers and landmarks. Only about 21 percent of residents worked in the city in 2000, and the Census puts the average commute today at 22.6 minutes.

sections.h2: What does recording a Fridley deed cost in Anoka County?
sections.html:
Anoka County records Fridley deeds, and its fee schedule effective July 1, 2025 lists a $46 recording fee for abstract property, a $5 conservation fee and a $54 well certificate. State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net consideration over $3,000. On a sale at Fridley's $302,900 median value, that is about $1,000.

Property tax payments go to Anoka County Property Records and Taxation at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, or online through PayAnokaCounty. The online system adds a 2.6 percent fee for cards and a $3.50 fee for e-checks, while checks and in-person payments at the Government Center carry no fee. State law splits the year's tax into two halves due before May 16 and October 16 (Minnesota Statutes 279.01), so the second half for 2026 has already come due.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fridley house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Often, yes, but check the notice first. The city can add abatement costs to the property's taxes, and buyers often ask for credits. A cash buyer takes the property as-is, while a retail buyer may ask you to fix flagged items first.

faqs.q: Who do I call to close my Fridley water account?
faqs.a: Call the Fridley Utility Billing Division at 763-572-3529 before closing. The city needs a meter reading on the closing date, and the closing date ends the seller's account and starts the buyer's.

faqs.q: How much is deed tax on a Fridley home sale?
faqs.a: It is 0.0033 of the net sale price once consideration exceeds $3,000. At $302,900, that is roughly $1,000. Anoka County collects it with a $5 conservation fee when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does the buyer of my Fridley rental need a rental license?
faqs.a: The city licenses rentals of one to three units and of four or more units, and a new owner applies through CitizenServe. The owner of record comes from Anoka County, so the application lets new owners upload purchase papers while that record catches up.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems with my Fridley house?
faqs.a: Yes. Before you sign a purchase agreement, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know that could significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment of the property. The disclosure must be made in good faith.
